authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: ZIM entered into a Merger Agreement with Hapag-Lloyd AG on February 16, 2026, under which Merger Sub (Norazia (Israel) Ltd.) will merge with and into ZIM, making ZIM a wholly owned subsidiary of Hapag-Lloyd AG, with merger consideration of $35.00 per ordinary share and a termination fee of $150,000,000.

The Israeli Government Companies Authority (GCA) determined to cease handling the pending application for approval of the requested changes in the Special State Share, which had been submitted in March 2026, after Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI failed to submit a detailed revised proposal by the GCA's deadline; Hapag-Lloyd stated it intends to submit a revised proposal.

ZIM raised its full-year 2026 guidance, increasing expected Adjusted EBITDA from between $2.0 billion and $2.4 billion to between $2.7 billion and $3.0 billion, and Adjusted EBIT from between $700 million and $1.1 billion to between $1.4 billion and $1.7 billion, citing continued strong market demand and favorable momentum in freight rates.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 4.B Business Overview)
business_model.claim: ZIM is a global container liner shipping company that transports cargo in containers via its fleet of vessels, with leadership positions in niche trade lanes.
quotes: We are a global container liner shipping company with leadership positions in niche markets where we believe we have distinct competitive advantages that allow us to maximize our market position and profitability.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 4.B)
business_model.claim: ZIM serves approximately 30,500 customers, with its 10 largest customers representing approximately 12% of freight revenues and its 50 largest representing approximately 27%.
quotes: We have a highly diverse and global customer base with approximately 30,500 customers (which considers each of our customer entities separately, including in instances where the entity is a subsidiary or branch of another customer, or on a non-consolidated basis) using our services.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 4.B)
business_model.claim: ZIM's operations are spread across five geographic trade zones by carried TEUs: Transpacific (43.0%), Intra-Asia (21.2%), Latin America (14.4%), Atlantic (13.5%), and Cross Suez (7.9%).
quotes: These trade zones include (for the year ended December 31, 2025, of carried TEUs): (1) Transpacific (43.0%), (2) Atlantic (13.5%), (3) Cross Suez (7.9%), (4) Intra-Asia (21.2%) and (5) Latin America (14.4%).

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, Item 5 – Factors affecting our results of operations)
business_model.claim: ZIM's revenue is driven by the volume of TEUs carried multiplied by the average freight rate per TEU, both of which are volatile and influenced by global trade conditions.
quotes: We measure our performance in terms of the volume of cargo we carry in a certain period in 20-foot equivalent units carried, or TEUs carried.
Average freight rate per TEU is calculated as revenues from containerized cargo during a certain period, divided by total TEUs carried during that period.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (P3 narrative; F2 income statement, table in millions)
business_model.claim: In 2025, ZIM carried 3,663 thousand TEUs and generated income from voyages and related services of $6,904.2 (table in millions), down from 3,751 thousand TEUs and $8,427.4 (table in millions) in 2024.
quotes: In the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we carried 3,663 thousand, 3,751 thousand and 3,281 thousand TEUs for our customers worldwide, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, Item 5)
business_model.claim: Cargo handling expenses (stevedoring, terminal, repositioning, inland transport) are the largest cost component, at 47.1% of operating expenses and cost of services in 2025.
quotes: Cargo handling accounted for 47.1%, 44.6% and 43.0% of our operating expenses and cost of services for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, Item 5)
business_model.claim: Bunker expenses (fuel and marine LNG) are the second-largest cost component, at 25.7% of operating expenses in 2025, and are sensitive to volatile fuel prices.
quotes: Our bunker expenses accounted for 25.7%, 28.5% and 28.3% of our operating expenses and cost of services for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 4.B)
business_model.claim: ZIM charters in 86.4% of its TEU capacity and 87.5% of its 128-vessel fleet, making its cost structure heavily dependent on time-charter hire rates rather than vessel ownership.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we operated a fleet of 128 vessels and chartered-in approximately 86.4% of our TEU capacity and 87.5% of the vessels in our fleet.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 4.B)
business_model.claim: In addition to container shipping, ZIM operates thirteen chartered car carrier vessels transporting vehicles westbound from Asia to ports in Europe, Central America, and South America.
quotes: Currently, we charter thirteen car carrier vessels and we serve ports in Europe (both North Europe and the Mediterranean), Central America and both coasts of South America.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 4.B)
business_model.claim: ZIM operates asset-light logistics subsidiaries (land transportation, customs brokerage, LCL, project cargo, air freight) in China, Canada, Brazil, India, Singapore, Hong Kong, and the U.S., with approximately 17% of TEUs utilizing additional land transportation.
quotes: Out of ZIM's total volume in the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, approximately 17% of our TEUs carried utilized additional elements of land transportation.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, Item 5 – Seasonality)
business_model.claim: ZIM's revenue is seasonal, typically higher in Q3 and Q4 due to pre-holiday consumer-goods shipments from Asia to North America, while operating expenses remain relatively fixed.
quotes: Our income from voyages and related services are typically higher in the third and fourth quarters than the first and second quarters due to increased shipping of consumer goods from manufacturing centers in Asia to North America in anticipation of the major holiday period in Western countries.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P2, Item 3.D Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: Freight rates are highly volatile: the SCFI index moved from 2,505 points on January 1, 2025 to 1,300 on April 1, 2025, then 2,000 on June 1, 2025, and 1,400 on December 31, 2025.
quotes: on January 1, 2025, the comprehensive Shanghai (Export) Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) started with 2,505 points, then dropped to 1,300 points on April 1, 2025, increased again to 2,000 points on June 1, 2025 and dropped back to 1,400 on December 31, 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, Item 5)
business_model.claim: Port and canal expenses (berthing, tug, sanitary services, Panama/Suez transit fees) accounted for 11.4% of operating expenses in 2025.
quotes: Our port (including canal) expenses accounted for 11.4%, 10.2% and 12.9% of our operating expenses and cost of services for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, Item 5)
business_model.claim: Personnel expenses (salaries, commissions, incentives in both operating and G&A) totaled $523.6 million in 2025, up from $496.8 million in 2024 and $428.3 million in 2023.
quotes: Personnel expenses, which comprise salaries, commissions and related expenses (including incentives) in both operating expenses and general and administrative expenses, totaled $523.6 million $496.8 million and $428.3 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

quotes: (1) Mediterranean to U.S. East Coast & Gulf t lane (Atlantic trade zone) where we maintain a 6.6% market share, (2) Far East to Mediterranean & Black Sea (Cross Suez trade zone), 7.5% market share, (3) Far East (not including the Indian subcontinent) to U.S. East Coast & Gulf (Pacific trade zone), 10.1% market share and (4) West Coast South America to USEC, 8.7% market share

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 4 Business Overview.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 4 Business Overview.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as a risk factor in the 20-F; the company acknowledges the competitive threat without quantifying specific rivals' advantages.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors as an ongoing condition.

material_events.claim: ZIM raised its full-year 2026 guidance, increasing expected Adjusted EBITDA from between $2.0 billion and $2.4 billion to between $2.7 billion and $3.0 billion, and Adjusted EBIT from between $700 million and $1.1 billion to between $1.4 billion and $1.7 billion, citing continued strong market demand and favorable momentum in freight rates.
quotes: ZIM now expects to generate Adjusted EBITDA of between $2.7 billion and $3.0 billion and Adjusted EBIT of between $1.4 billion and $1.7 billion for the full year 2026, compared with its previous guidance of Adjusted EBITDA between $2.0 billion and $2.4 billion and Adjusted EBIT between $700 million and $1.1 billion.
